11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.

## 1. The scent, the shirt and the reunion  (`#the-scent-the-shirt-and-the-reunion`)

Cited ayat: 12:94-101

### Claims

**c1** (12:94): When the caravan set out, their father said that he found the scent of Yusuf, unless they thought him weak-minded.

**c2** (12:95): Others said that, by God, he was in his old error.

**c3** (12:96): When the bearer of good news came, he cast the shirt on the father's face, and the father returned seeing; he said, did he not tell them that he knew from God what they did not know.

**c4** (12:97-98): His sons asked their father to ask forgiveness for their sins, since they had been sinners, and he said he would ask forgiveness for them from his Lord, who is forgiving and merciful.

**c5** (12:99): When they entered on Yusuf, he took his parents to himself and told them to enter Egypt, if God willed, in safety.

**c6** (12:100): Yusuf raised his parents upon the throne, and they fell down before him in prostration; he said that this was the interpretation of his dream of before, which his Lord had made true.

**c7** (12:100): Yusuf said that his Lord had been good to him in bringing him out of the prison and in bringing them from the desert, after Satan had stirred up enmity between him and his brothers; his Lord is subtle in what He wills, the knowing, the wise.

**c8** (12:101): Yusuf prayed that God, who had given him of the kingdom and taught him the interpretation of events, and who is the creator of the heavens and the earth, would take him as one who submits and join him with the righteous.

### One-minute summary

Their father said he found the scent of Yusuf, and when the shirt was cast on his face he returned seeing [c1][c3]. Yusuf took his parents to himself, and they fell down before him in prostration, and he said this was the interpretation of his dream of before [c5][c6].

### Complete story

When the caravan set out, their father said that he found the scent of Yusuf, unless they thought him weak-minded [c1]. Others said that, by God, he was in his old error [c2]. When the bearer of good news came, he cast the shirt on the father's face, and the father returned seeing [c3]. His sons asked him to ask forgiveness for their sins, and he said he would ask forgiveness for them from his Lord [c4].

When they entered on Yusuf, he took his parents to himself and told them to enter Egypt, if God willed, in safety [c5]. He raised his parents upon the throne, and they fell down before him in prostration; he said that this was the interpretation of his dream of before, which his Lord had made true [c6]. He said that his Lord had been good to him in bringing him out of the prison and bringing them from the desert, after Satan had stirred up enmity between him and his brothers [c7].

Yusuf prayed that God would take him as one who submits and join him with the righteous [c8].

### Deep study

The chapter joins movements: the scent and the shirt [c1][c2][c3], the forgiveness asked from the father [c4] and the meeting with its prostration, with Yusuf's words about the dream [c5][c6][c7]. It ends with his prayer [c8]. The verses do not say who the parents are, and the sense of the Arabic verb in the prayer, the one used for taking a soul, is read in more than one way [c8].

### Kids mode

Their father said he could smell Yusuf [c1]. When the shirt was put on his face, he could see again [c3]. Yusuf's parents bowed before him, and he said this was the meaning of his old dream [c6].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that Yusuf names the fulfilled dream as his Lord's doing and speaks of Satan's part in the enmity [c6][c7]. Another is that the chapter ends with a prayer to be taken as one who submits [c8].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: how much time passed between the first dream and the reunion; Yusuf calls the dream one of before.
- The verses do not say who the others are in 12:95.
- The verses do not say who the parents of 12:99-100 are; later accounts differ and none is used here.
- The father is not named in these verses.
- The Quran does not say what the prostration was, whether greeting, honour or something else.
- The Arabic verb in Yusuf's prayer (12:101) is the one used for taking a soul; how to render it is left to the reviewer.
- Not established: what became of the brothers, or Yusuf's death.
